question.problem:
Given that 
$A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ -2 & -6\end{aligned}]$
has the LU decomposition $A=LU$, then ${l}_{21}+{u}_{22}=$
question.worked_solution:
We need to reduce the matrix to the row echelon form. For every elementary row operation we also write the equivalent notation in terms of multiplication by the corresponding elementary matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ -2 & -6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1}\,⟺\,\overset{{E}_{1}}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]}}\cdot A \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =U\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix is upper triangular, so it is our matrix $U.$ Now, since ${E}_{1}A=U,$ we can invert ${E}_{1}$ to arrive at the desired LU factorization:

$$
\begin{aligned}{E}_{1}A & =U \\ A & ={E}_{1}^{-1}U \\ A & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}U \\ A & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{L}{{[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{U}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ${l}_{21}=-2,{u}_{22}=0,$ and ${l}_{21}+{u}_{22}=-2.$
